title: Unit tests that assert_applied(ruling=...) for R-01 (creation tool proficiency), R-02 (XP split), R-03 (encounter budget GM-only / blocked reinforcements) and R-04 (disarm without Thieves' Tools); only R-05..R-07 are covered by the new traceability tests

history.summary:
I added unit tests that call `game.log.assert_applied(ruling=...)` for R-01 to R-04. Each ruling has a positive test (the ruling is logged, with the right page and visibility) and a negative test (no ruling is logged when the case doesn't come up):
- **R-01:** Lidda's duplicate Thieves' Tools is replaced by a Disguise Kit, and the prompt asking for a replacement cites R-01. Brom, whose tools don't overlap, logs nothing.
- **R-02:** 250 XP split among 3 PCs gives 83 each, logged on page 255.
- **R-03:** an over-High rating is logged GM-only with R-03 and adds no player event. A rating inside the budget logs no ruling. Reinforcements without a justification are refused with ruling R-03 and page 202. With a justification they're logged GM-only. Reinforcements within budget log nothing.
- **R-04:** disarming without Thieves' Tools is a single-d20 check, logged GM-only with R-04 on page 94. Disarming with the tools logs no ruling.

To meet the page requirement for log events, I also added `page=` to the two ruling events that had none: R-01 in `creation.py` (page 83, from ORIGIN…tool-proficiency) and R-04 in `traps.py` (page 94, from EQUIP…thieves-tools-25-gp). I didn't add SRD tags because the ticket has no analysed unit.

Results: the full suite passes (560 tests), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` are clean, and the dev-gate passes. The ticket names no acceptance tests, so there was nothing to run with `--runxfail`.
